brief: TME argues the AI bull case keeps strengthening (frontier models solving previously unsolved problems, Google Cloud deals growing over 2x QoQ/YoY, Broadcom demand exceeding its $115bn FY27 outlook) while the tape simultaneously flashes macro stress: the yen is strengthening on priced BOJ tightening and repatriation, tech CDS spreads have widened since mid-August, and rates have moved higher, yet NDX has not broken down. The note frames the bear case as capture-of-economics risk, not demand, and argues that if tech breaks, the catalyst would be macro rates, yen strength and leverage draining via a yen-funded carry unwind rather than weak demand. Six-month realized SPX correlation has fallen to 11, a level seen only twice in 25 years, February 2007 and January 2018, ahead of Volmageddon, and SPX straddles sit near yearly lows. Garrett argues such correlation extremes rarely persist and typically resolve in an explosive return of vol convexity. The note concludes convexity is cheap and recommends long SPX straddles as a two-sided expression of the eventual break, with BofA preferring a more targeted hedge: sell the October 16 VIX put, buy the November 22-30 call spread.
